maria: Quick heads-up — I sketched a hedged burst pool design to reduce our spot risk without sacrificing >50% of current cost savings. TL;DR: keep a small on-demand floor per-region + predictive short-lived spot burst capacity + fast warm fallback. Posting details and questions.

devon: Sounds interesting — mind sketching the math for the floor? :thinking:

maria: Sure. Main constraints: (1) global latency SLAs per-customer (p50/p99), (2) budgeted cost delta <= +20% worst-case, (3) ability to absorb 15–30% spot interruptions without user-visible errors.

maria: Proposal steps:
- Per-region, compute "safe floor" = max(historical peak 5m baseline, 20% of peak forecast) but not exceeding N GPUs per-customer cap. Formula: `floor = max(peak5m, 0.2 * forecast_peak)`
- Maintain a small hot pool of on-demand nodes sized to floor. These are always warm (no cold-start).
- Add a predictive spot-burst group: autoscaler spins spot nodes when short-term demand > floor. Use ML-ish short-term predictor (last 10 min, EWMA) to pre-launch 90s before expected need.
- Hedging: for each burst batch, allocate across at least 2 AZs and mix instance types to reduce correlated preemptions.

aj: Do we have historical preempt rates by AZ? We should avoid AZs that spike more during our peak windows.

maria: Yes, SRE telemetry has per-AZ preempt probability histograms. Proposed default: avoid AZs where probability > 0.35 for 30m window unless necessary.

ashley: How do we handle the pretty common short preemption wave (like 1–3 min windows) — do we drain or migrate?

maria: Two-layer strategy: (A) Best-effort live-migration for reservation-aware workloads (checkpoint & resume), (B) fast fallback routing for ephemeral requests. For (B) we replicate small inference workers on the on-demand floor with tiny warm caches so failover cost is minimal.

ravi: Need specifics on node packing and KV-cache duplication. If we replicate caches on the floor, memory overhead could be big.

maria: Agree. Plan: replicate only last-2-turn KV caches for chat-style sessions on the floor. Full KV cache stays on spot; we accept increased latency on a miss during failover. We can also use a tiny shared Redis for cold-start keys as intermediate cache.

devon: Autoscaler config idea?

maria: Suggested HPA-style config snippet: 
```yaml
name: hedged-spot-burst
minReplicas: 0
maxReplicas: 120
scaleTrigger:
  - type: pending-requests
    threshold: 30
prelaunchWindowSec: 90
placementPolicy:
  azSpread: true
  mixInstanceTypes: true
  maxPerAz: 0.6 # fraction when bursting
```

aj: prelaunchWindowSec 90 feels aggressive — do we have observed startup times that justify it? cold boot + model load often 60–120s on our instances.

maria: We measured warm-start path (container warm, model cached) ~15s; cold-start (node spin + load) median 85s. 90s leaves a small buffer. We can tune by model size group.

ashley: What about cost controls — we don't want bursts to blow budgets in unexpected demand spikes.

maria: We'll add: (1) per-customer burst budget cap (by $/hour), (2) system-wide emergency cap to throttle bursts, (3) soft-fallback to lower-cost model variants (quantized) if budget/throttle activates.

ravi: Operational playbooks? If spot wave hits multiple AZs at once, what's oncall's immediate runbook?

maria: Draft runbook: 
- oncall-bot posts interruption metrics + region map (auto)
- if interruption > 10% sustained for 10m -> escalate to infra lead
- infra lead can flip policy: increase local floor (auto-raise using reserved instances) or reroute traffic to other regions (with traffic-shift window)
- fallback model QOS knob: `ramp_quantized=true`

oncall-bot: Incident detected: us-west-2 spot preempt sequence started at 2026-02-11T16:12:00Z, 14 nodes terminated in 4m. Posting telemetry: https://telemetry/internal/spot/1791234567

devon: Nice, the runbook looks solid. One more thought: can we use short-lived reserved capacity for predictable nightly batch bursts? those are cost-effective vs on-demand.

maria: Yes — for predictable windows we can pre-buy short-term reservations (1–7 days) or use convertible reserved capacity where available. We'll add a scheduling hint for batch jobs so autoscaler can choose reserved-backed nodes first.

ashley: Any changes needed to routing layer? How do we ensure requests that require model version X get to nodes with X loaded (especially during failover)?

maria: Router will maintain a model-hotness map: node -> models-in-memory TTL. For failover, routing prefers nodes where model is hot; if none, route to on-demand floor with guaranteed model-load pool (a small set pinned per popular model).

aj: Action items?

maria: Action list: 
- devon: prototype predictor using last-10m EWMA and output prelaunch decisions (due EOD +2)
- ravi: evaluate memory overhead of KV-lite replicate + Redis config (due +3)
- ashley: test preemption playbook in chaos window (dry-run) next Tuesday
- aj: cost model sim for worst-case +20% cap (due +4)

devon: Acked, I'll start a small sim with our historical traffic.

ravi: I'll baseline KV-lite memory numbers and share a config patch.

ashley: I'll schedule the chaos dry-run and invite infra & serving teams.

maria: Thanks all — I'll update the design doc and add the autoscaler PR draft. :thumbsup:

devon: small nit — maybe call it "hedged burst" in the doc, not "hedge burst" :)

maria: Fixed in doc.
